title: Peanut Butter Rice Crispies
steps: Butter a 9x13 pan.
Bring the corn syrup and sugar to a full boil in a large pot over medium heat, stirring. Take it off the heat as soon as it boils.
Stir in the peanut butter until smooth, then fold in the cereal until coated.
Press firmly into the pan with buttered hands.
For the topping, melt the butterscotch and chocolate chips together, spread over the bars, and let set 1 hour before cutting.

title: French Toast

ingredients.name: slices thick Texas toast or day-old bread
maple syrup and powdered sugar to serve

steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in a shallow dish.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium and melt a pat of butter.
Dip each slice for about 10 seconds per side so it soaks through without falling apart.
Cook 2–3 minutes per side until golden, adding butter as needed.
Serve hot with butter, syrup and a dusting of powdered sugar.

title: Homemade Chili
steps: Brown the beef in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat; drain most of the fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the spices, salt, pepper and tomato paste and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, sauce, beans, broth and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer, cover partly and cook 1 hour, stirring now and then.
Stir in the masa or cornmeal and simmer 10 more minutes to thicken. Taste and adjust salt and heat.
Serve with shredded cheddar, onions, sour cream, Fritos or cornbread.

title: Cheeseburger

ingredients.name: Burger Seasoning Blend (or salt and pepper)
lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles to serve
Special Sauce or ketchup and mustard

steps: Divide the beef into 4 balls and press into patties a little wider than the buns, with a thumbprint dimple in the center.
Season both sides generously right before cooking.
Cook on a hot cast iron skillet or grill 3–4 minutes per side for medium.
Top with cheese for the last minute and cover to melt.
Butter and toast the buns, then build with sauce, lettuce, tomato, onion and pickles.

title: Fried Green Tomatoes
steps: Salt the tomato slices and let them sit 15 minutes on paper towels, then pat dry.
Whisk the buttermilk and egg. In another dish mix the flour, cornmeal, salt, pepper, cayenne and garlic powder.
Dip each slice in buttermilk, then press into the cornmeal mixture to coat.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 350°F for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with salt. Serve hot with Comeback or ranch.

title: Steak Nachos

ingredients.name: Classic Yellow Cheese Dip (or 3 cups shredded cheese)
pico de gallo, pickled jalapeños, sour cream, guacamole, cilantro

steps: Rub the steak with the spices, salt and lime juice and rest 15 minutes.
Sear in a very hot skillet or grill 4–5 minutes per side to medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes and slice thin against the grain, then chop.
Spread chips on a sheet pan, scatter beans and steak, and warm in a 400°F oven 5 minutes.
Pour warm cheese dip over the top and finish with pico, jalapeños, sour cream, guacamole and cilantro.

title: Classic Yellow Cheese Dip

ingredients.name: (10 oz) Rotel diced tomatoes and green chiles, drained

steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat and whisk in the flour for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cook until slightly thickened, 3–4 minutes.
Add the American cheese a handful at a time, stirring until melted, then the cheddar.
Stir in the spices, Rotel and jalapeño juice. Thin with milk if it gets too thick.
Keep warm on low or in a small slow cooker. Serve with tortilla chips.
notes: Arkansas is the cheese dip state — it was first served at Mexico Chiquito in Hot Springs in 1935.

title: White Cheese Dip

ingredients.name: white American cheese from the deli, chopped
pickled jalapeños, minced, plus 2 tbsp juice

steps: Put the American cheese, milk and butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Stir constantly until smooth — don't let it boil or it will break.
Stir in the green chiles, jalapeños and juice, cumin, garlic powder and cayenne.
Add the Monterey Jack and stir until melted. Thin with a splash of milk as needed.
Serve warm with tortilla chips.

title: Blackened Burger
steps: Make 4 patties and coat both sides heavily with the Cajun seasoning.
Heat a cast iron skillet until smoking (open a window). Brush the patties with melted butter.
Cook 3–4 minutes per side until a dark crust forms. Add cheese at the end and cover to melt.
Stir the mayo, Creole mustard and hot sauce together.
Toast the buns and build with the sauce, lettuce, tomato and onion.

title: Arkansas Cajun Seasoning Blend
steps: Mix everything well and store in an airtight jar for up to 6 months.
Use on fish, chicken, burgers, fries and in dirty rice.

title: Homemade Thousand Island Dressing
steps: Stir everything together until smooth.
Chill at least 30 minutes so the flavors come together. Keeps 1 week refrigerated.
Use on salads, Patty Melts and Reubens.

title: Black Bean Burger

ingredients.name: (15 oz) black beans, drained, rinsed and patted dry

steps: Spread the beans on a sheet pan and bake at 325°F for 15 minutes to dry them out.
Mash the beans, leaving some chunks. Mix in the panko, egg, onion, garlic, corn, spices, salt and barbecue sauce.
Form 4 patties and chill 15 minutes to firm up.
Cook in hot oil 4–5 minutes per side until crisp. Add cheese at the end if you like.
Serve on toasted buns with your favorite toppings.

title: Nachos

ingredients.name: pico de gallo, jalapeños, sour cream, shredded lettuce, black olives

steps: Brown the beef, drain, and simmer with taco seasoning and 2/3 cup water until thick.
Layer chips on a platter or sheet pan with spoonfuls of refried beans and the beef.
Pour warm cheese dip over everything.
Top with pico, jalapeños, lettuce, olives and sour cream. Serve right away.

title: Homemade Blue Cheese Dressing
steps: Whisk the mayo, sour cream, buttermilk, lemon juice, Worcestershire, garlic powder and pepper.
Fold in the blue cheese, mashing some of it against the bowl.
Chill 1 hour. Keeps 1 week. Great with wings and wedge salads.

title: Fried Jalapeños and Pickles

ingredients.name: (24 oz) dill pickle chips, drained and patted dry
sliced jalapeños (fresh or pickled), patted dry

steps: Heat 2 inches of oil to 375°F.
Whisk the buttermilk and egg. Mix the flour, cornmeal, Cajun seasoning and garlic powder.
Dip pickles and jalapeños in buttermilk, then dredge in the flour mix.
Fry in small batches 2–3 minutes until golden. Drain and salt lightly.
Serve hot with ranch.
notes: Fried dill pickles were made famous by the Duchess Drive-In in Atkins, Arkansas, in 1963.

title: Burger Seasoning Blend
steps: Mix and store airtight. Use about 1 tsp per pound of beef, sprinkled on right before cooking.

title: Twice Baked Potatoes
steps: Rub the potatoes with oil and salt and bake at 400°F for 1 hour until tender.
Cool 10 minutes, halve lengthwise and scoop the insides into a bowl, leaving a thin shell.
Mash with sour cream, butter, milk, 1 cup cheddar, most of the bacon and green onions, salt and pepper.
Pile back into the skins and top with the remaining cheese and bacon.
Bake at 400°F for 15–20 minutes until hot and bubbly. Garnish with green onions.

title: Meatloaf with Mashed Potatoes and White Gravy
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Soak the crackers in the milk for 5 minutes.
Mix in the beef, eggs, onion, Worcestershire, salt, pepper and garlic powder with your hands just until combined.
Shape into a loaf on a foil-lined sheet pan.
Stir the ketchup, brown sugar and mustard and spread half over the loaf.
Bake 1 hour, spread on the rest of the glaze, and bake 15 minutes more until it reads 160°F inside.
Rest 10 minutes, slice, and serve with mashed potatoes and white gravy.

title: Fried Fish

ingredients.name: white fish fillets (catfish, cod or crappie)
peanut or vegetable oil for frying

steps: Soak the fish in buttermilk and hot sauce for 30 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour and seasonings in a shallow dish.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F.
Lift the fish from the buttermilk, let it drip, and press into the cornmeal coating.
Fry 4–5 minutes, turning once, until golden and flaky. Drain on a rack and salt right away.
Serve with lemon, tartar sauce, hushpuppies and coleslaw.

title: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
steps: Soup: melt the butter and cook the onion 5 minutes, then the garlic 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar and basil and simmer 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and salt, and keep warm.
Sandwiches: butter the outsides of the bread, fill with cheese, and cook in a skillet over medium-low 3–4 minutes per side until golden and melted.
Cut on the diagonal and serve with the soup for dunking.

title: Cajun Chicken Alfredo

ingredients.name: parsley and green onion to garnish

steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted water; save 1 cup pasta water before draining.
Toss the chicken with 1 1/2 tbsp Cajun seasoning and sear in oil over medium-high 5–6 minutes until cooked. Set aside.
In the same pan melt the butter, cook the pepper 2 minutes and the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the cream and remaining seasoning and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in the Parmesan until smooth.
Toss in the pasta and chicken, loosening with pasta water. Garnish and serve.

title: Fried Potatoes

ingredients.name: russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut in 1/2-inch pieces

steps: Heat the grease and butter in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high.
Add the potatoes in an even layer and leave them alone 5 minutes to brown.
Turn, add the onion, cover and cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Uncover and cook 5 more minutes to crisp. Season with salt, pepper and paprika.

title: BLT

ingredients.name: large ripe tomato, sliced (Bradley County pink tomatoes in summer)

steps: Cook the bacon in a skillet or at 400°F in the oven until crisp. Drain.
Spread mayo generously on the toast.
Salt and pepper the tomato slices.
Layer lettuce, tomato and bacon, close, and cut in half.

title: Chicken Fried Ribeye Steak

ingredients.name: ribeye steaks (about 10 oz each), pounded to 1/2 inch

steps: Season the steaks with salt and pepper.
Whisk the buttermilk, egg and hot sauce. Mix the flour with garlic powder, paprika and cayenne.
Dredge each steak in flour, dip in buttermilk, then back in flour, pressing to coat. Rest 10 minutes.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 350°F for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Make the gravy in the same skillet using 1/3 cup of the frying oil. Smother and serve with mashed potatoes.

title: Peanut Butter Cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Beat the butter, peanut butter and sugars until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Roll into 1-inch balls, roll in sugar and press a crisscross with a fork.
Bake 9–10 minutes until just set. Cool on the pan 5 minutes.

title: Orange Chicken

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut in 1-inch pieces
cooked white rice and green onions

steps: Toss the chicken in beaten egg, then in the cornstarch, flour and salt.
Fry in 2 inches of oil at 350°F for 4–5 minutes until crisp and cooked. Drain.
Simmer the juice, zest, sugar, soy, vinegar, garlic, ginger and pepper flakes 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and serve over rice with green onions.

title: Ribeye Steak with Baked Potato

ingredients.name: butter, sour cream, cheddar, bacon and chives for the potatoes

steps: Potatoes: rub with oil and salt and bake at 425°F for 55–60 minutes until tender.
Season the steaks with salt and pepper 40 minutes ahead and let them come to room temperature.
Sear in a smoking-hot cast iron skillet with oil, 4 minutes per side.
Add the butter, garlic and herbs and spoon the butter over the steaks for 1–2 minutes, to 130°F for medium-rare.
Rest 8 minutes. Split the potatoes and load them up.

title: Spicy Marinara Meat Sauce
steps: Brown the beef and sausage in olive oil, breaking it up. Drain most of the fat.
Add the onion and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then deglaze with the wine.
Add the tomatoes, sauce, herbs, sugar, salt, pepper and Parmesan rind.
Simmer uncovered on low 1 1/2 hours, stirring often. Serve over pasta.

title: Chicken Spaghetti
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13 dish. Cook the spaghetti 2 minutes short of done.
Melt the butter and cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes, then the garlic.
Stir in both soups, Rotel, Velveeta, broth and seasoning until the cheese melts.
Fold in the chicken and spaghetti and spread in the dish. Top with cheddar.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbly.

title: Blackened Fish

ingredients.name: fillets catfish, redfish or tilapia (6 oz each)

steps: Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot, about 5 minutes. Turn on the vent.
Dip each fillet in melted butter and coat both sides heavily with seasoning.
Lay in the dry skillet and cook 2–3 minutes per side until a black crust forms and the fish flakes.
Drizzle a little butter over the top and serve with lemon.

title: Spam and Rice
steps: Fry the Spam slices in a dry nonstick skillet over medium-high 2–3 minutes per side until browned.
Mix the soy sauce, brown sugar and water, pour over the Spam and cook until sticky and glazed.
Serve over rice with a fried egg and green onions.

title: Biscuits and White Gravy

ingredients.name: breakfast sausage (such as Jimmy Dean or Petit Jean)

steps: Bake the biscuits.
Brown the sausage in a cast iron skillet, breaking it up. Don't drain.
Sprinkle the flour over the sausage and stir 2 minutes.
Slowly pour in the milk, stirring, and bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
Season with plenty of pepper, salt and cayenne. Split the biscuits and ladle gravy over.

title: Fried Chicken Sandwich
steps: Marinate the chicken in buttermilk, pickle juice and hot sauce for at least 1 hour.
Mix the flour, powdered sugar and spices. Drizzle in 2 tbsp of the marinade and rub in to make shaggy bits.
Dredge the chicken, pressing hard so the coating sticks.
Fry at 350°F for 6–7 minutes until 175°F inside.
Build on toasted buns with mayo and plenty of pickles.

title: Deviled Eggs
steps: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, cover, turn off the heat and let sit 12 minutes. Move to ice water.
Peel, halve lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with mayo, mustard, relish, pickle juice, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spoon or pipe back into the whites and dust with paprika. Chill until serving.

title: Scrambled Eggs
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and salt until no streaks remain.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low.
Add the eggs and let them sit 20 seconds, then push slowly with a spatula to form big soft curds.
Take off the heat while still a little glossy; they'll finish cooking. Add cheese and pepper.

title: Ground Beef Tacos

ingredients.name: shredded lettuce, cheddar, diced tomato, onion, sour cream, salsa

steps: Brown the beef and drain.
Add the spices, salt and cornstarch, then the water. Simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Warm the shells in the oven.
Fill and top with lettuce, cheese, tomato, onion, sour cream and salsa.

title: Veggie Tacos

ingredients.name: large sweet potato, peeled and cut in 1/2-inch cubes
avocado, cotija, cilantro, lime, pickled onions

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sweet potato, pepper and onion with oil, spices and salt.
Roast 25 minutes, stirring once, until browned. Stir in the beans for the last 5 minutes.
Fill warm tortillas and top with avocado, cotija, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

title: Bean and Cheese Burrito

ingredients.name: Classic Yellow Cheese Dip (optional, for smothering)

steps: Warm the beans with the salsa and cumin.
Warm the tortillas so they fold without tearing.
Spread beans down the center, top with cheese, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Toast seam-side down in a dry skillet 2 minutes per side. Smother with cheese dip if you like.

title: Fried Zucchini
steps: Salt the zucchini, rest 10 minutes and pat dry.
Dredge in flour, dip in buttermilk, then coat in panko mixed with Parmesan and seasonings.
Fry at 350°F 2 minutes per side until golden. Drain and salt. Serve with marinara or ranch.

title: Au Gratin Potatoes

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes, sliced 1/8 inch thick

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a 9x13 dish.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and garlic for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cream. Simmer until thick.
Off the heat, stir in half the cheese, the salt, pepper and thyme.
Layer the potatoes and sauce in thirds, ending with sauce, and top with the remaining cheese.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes, uncover and bake 30 minutes more until browned and tender. Rest 15 minutes.

title: Baked Potatoes

ingredients.name: butter, sour cream, cheddar, bacon, chives

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Scrub and dry the potatoes and poke each a few times with a fork.
Rub with oil and kosher salt and set directly on the oven rack.
Bake 50–60 minutes until a knife slides in easily and the skin is crisp.
Split, fluff with a fork and load up.

title: Mashed Potatoes

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut in 2-inch chunks
cream cheese or 1/2 cup sour cream

steps: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water, bring to a boil and cook 15–20 minutes until very tender.
Drain well and return to the hot pot for 1 minute to dry out.
Mash with the butter, then the cream cheese, then add the warm milk a little at a time.
Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm in a slow cooker on low for the holidays.

title: French Fries

ingredients.name: peanut or vegetable oil for frying

steps: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water 30 minutes, then dry thoroughly.
Fry at 300°F in batches for 5 minutes until limp and pale. Drain and rest 15 minutes.
Raise the oil to 375°F and fry again 2–3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain, salt immediately and serve.

title: Special Sauce
steps: Stir everything together and chill 30 minutes. Keeps 1 week.
Use on burgers, fries and fried chicken sandwiches.

title: Tartar Sauce
steps: Mix everything and chill at least 30 minutes. Keeps 1 week. Serve with fried fish and catfish.

title: Sour Cream Horseradish Sauce
steps: Stir together and chill 1 hour. Serve with steak, prime rib and roast beef sandwiches.

title: Patty Melt
steps: Cook the onion in 1 tbsp butter over medium-low 20 minutes until deep golden.
Shape the beef into 2 thin oval patties the size of the bread, season and sear 2–3 minutes per side.
Spread dressing on the bread and layer cheese, patty, onions and cheese.
Butter the outsides and toast in a skillet over medium 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and melted.

title: Hoppin' John (Without Pork)

ingredients.name: hot sauce and green onions to serve

steps: Using the sauté setting, cook the onion, pepper and celery in oil 5 minutes, then the garlic and spices 1 minute.
Add the peas, bay leaf, broth and salt.
Pressure cook on high 10 minutes for firm peas (14 for soft) with a 10-minute natural release.
Discard the bay leaf, adjust salt, and serve over rice with hot sauce and green onions.
notes: Eat it on New Year's Day for luck, with collard greens for money.

title: Coconut-Milk Braised Turkey with Rice

ingredients.name: turkey thighs or breast, cut in 2-inch pieces
(13.5 oz) coconut milk (or chicken stock plus a splash of cream)

steps: Season the turkey and brown it in oil in a Dutch oven. Set aside.
Cook the onion 5 minutes, then the garlic, ginger and curry powder 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, broth and brown sugar, return the turkey, and simmer covered 35–40 minutes until tender.
Stir in the lime juice and serve over rice with cilantro and scallions.

title: Turkey French Dip with Slaw
steps: Simmer the broth with Worcestershire and garlic powder for the jus.
Toss the cabbage with mayo, vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt for the slaw.
Warm the turkey in the jus for 1 minute.
Pile turkey on the rolls with provolone and slaw, and serve with cups of jus for dipping.

title: Ultimate Seafood Fondue

ingredients.name: bread cubes and tortilla chips for dipping

steps: Melt the butter and soften the onion and garlic 3 minutes. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk and wine and simmer until thick.
Stir in the cream cheese, then the Swiss and Jack until smooth.
Fold in the shrimp, crab, Old Bay and cayenne. Keep warm in a fondue pot or slow cooker and serve with bread and chips.

title: Red Wine Braised Pork Chops with Garlic
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a heavy skillet over high heat. Salt and pepper the chops and sear about 2 minutes per side until golden. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium-high, add the garlic cloves and cook 2 minutes, stirring, until they start to color.
Pour in the wine and broth, add the bay leaf and balsamic, and scrape up the browned bits. Boil 3 minutes.
Return the chops, cover, and simmer on low 20–25 minutes until tender, adding broth if it gets dry.
Move the chops to a platter, boil the sauce until syrupy, swirl in the extra tablespoon of butter and pour over the chops with the soft garlic.

title: Baked Mac and Cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13 dish. Toss the cooked macaroni with the olive oil.
Melt the 6 tbsp butter, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and cream and simmer until thick, about 5 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in 3 cups cheddar and 1 1/2 cups Gruyère until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Fold in the macaroni and pour half into the dish. Sprinkle with the remaining cheddar and Gruyère, add the rest of the pasta.
Toss the panko with melted butter, Parmesan and paprika and scatter over the top.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbly and golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Ground Beef Stroganoff
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms and onions 6–8 minutes until browned. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink. Drain excess fat.
Stir in 1 cup of the broth, the Worcestershire, salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Whisk the flour into the remaining broth, stir it in and simmer 2 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, stir in the sour cream. Serve over the noodles with parsley.

title: Steak Stroganoff
steps: Cook the noodles, drain and toss with 1 tbsp butter.
Season the steak with salt and pepper and sear in 1 tbsp butter in a hot skillet in batches, 1 minute per side. Set aside.
Melt the remaining butter and cook the onion and mushrooms 8 minutes until browned, then the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the wine and reduce by half. Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute, then add the stock and Worcestershire and simmer until thick.
Lower the heat, stir in the yogurt or sour cream and return the steak to warm through. Serve over the noodles with parsley.

title: Easy Vegetable Stir Fry
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, chicken broth and cornstarch together for the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the carrots and broccoli and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, baby corn and water chestnuts and cook 2 minutes more, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy and thick, about 1 minute.
Top with green onions and sesame seeds and serve over rice.

title: Classic Shepherd's Pie
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, drain, and mash with the butter, half and half, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Stir in the Parmesan.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Cook the onion in olive oil 5 minutes, add the beef and brown it, then drain.
Stir in the herbs, salt, pepper, Worcestershire and garlic, then the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the broth, peas and carrots and corn and simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Spread the filling in a 2-quart baking dish and top with the potatoes, roughing up the surface with a fork.
Bake 25 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes.

title: Sweet Cornbread
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and grease a 9x13 pan.
Beat the margarine and sugar until creamy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in another bowl.
Add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk, mixing just until combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 22–25 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

title: Favorite Chicken Potpie
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Boil the potatoes and carrots 8–10 minutes until crisp-tender and drain.
Melt the butter and cook the onion until soft. Stir in the flour, salt, thyme and pepper until blended.
Gradually stir in the broth and milk, bring to a boil and cook 2 minutes until thick.
Stir in the chicken, peas, corn, potatoes and carrots.
Line two 9-inch pie plates with crust, divide the filling, and top with the remaining crusts. Crimp and cut slits.
Bake 35–40 minutes until golden. Rest 15 minutes. Freeze the second pie unbaked if you like.

title: Apple Crisp
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter an 8x8 or 9-inch baking dish.
Toss the apples with the granulated sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and the lemon juice and spread in the dish.
Mix the brown sugar, oats, flour, remaining cinnamon and salt, then work in the cold butter with your fingers until crumbly.
Scatter the topping over the apples.
Bake 40–45 minutes until bubbling and golden. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

title: Beef Stew
steps: Pat the beef dry, season with half the salt and 1 tsp pepper, and toss with the flour.
Brown the beef in the oil in a Dutch oven in batches. Set aside.
Cook the onions 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then deglaze with the wine.
Return the beef with the broth, vinegar, bay leaf, thyme and remaining salt. Cover and simmer on low 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer 30–40 minutes more until tender. Remove the bay leaf and garnish with parsley.

title: Roasted Garlic Cream Sauce
steps: Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of their skins and mash to a paste.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and stir in the garlic and flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in the 1 3/4 cups cream and simmer gently 3–4 minutes until slightly thick.
Stir in the Parmesan and pepper until smooth, loosening with the extra tablespoon of cream. Toss with pasta or spoon over chicken.

title: Easy Fried Rice
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Scramble the eggs with the salt and pepper, then set aside.
Melt 2 tbsp butter and cook the onion 3 minutes.
Add the remaining butter and the cold rice, pressing it into the pan, and fry 3–4 minutes without stirring too much.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil and eggs and toss until hot.

title: Creamy Mushroom Sauce
steps: Melt the butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and garlic until translucent.
Add the mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and cook until browned and their liquid evaporates, 6–8 minutes.
Pour in the wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the broth and cream and simmer 3–4 minutes until thick, then stir in the Parmesan and cayenne. Serve over chicken, steak or pasta.

title: Maple Pecan Latte
steps: Sauce: simmer the maple syrup, brown sugar, cream and butter 3 minutes, then whisk in the vanilla, pecan butter, condensed milk and salt until smooth. Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated.
Brew the espresso into a mug and stir in 2–3 tbsp of the sauce.
Steam or froth the milk and pour it over.
Top with whipped cream, a drizzle of sauce and chopped pecans.

title: Grilled Ribs with Dry Rub
steps: Mix the rub. Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs and coat both sides heavily with rub. Rest 1 hour or overnight.
Set up the grill for indirect heat at 250–275°F, ideally with hickory wood.
Cook the ribs bone-side down for 3 hours, spritzing with apple juice every hour.
Wrap in foil with a splash of apple juice and cook 1 more hour until tender.
Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and cook 15–20 minutes to set the glaze. Rest 10 minutes and slice.

title: Creamy Mustard Sauce with Spinach
steps: Cook the onion in a little butter over medium heat 5 minutes, then the garlic 1 minute.
Add the half and half and chicken stock and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the onion powder, garlic powder and both mustards.
Add the spinach a handful at a time until wilted. Simmer 2 minutes and spoon over salmon or chicken.

title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
steps: Heat the oil in a soup pot and cook the onion, garlic and jalapeño 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin and chili powder.
Add the chicken breasts, tomatoes and broth. Simmer covered 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it with the beans, corn and half the cilantro. Simmer 5 minutes.
Tortilla strips: slice the tortillas thin and fry in the olive oil until crisp. Salt.
Stir in the lime juice and salt. Serve topped with strips, avocado, cheese and the remaining cilantro.

title: Southern Potato Salad
steps: Cover the potatoes with cold water and the 2 tsp salt, bring to a boil and cook 10–12 minutes until just tender. Drain and cool 15 minutes.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, pickle juice, salt and pepper.
Fold in the potatoes, eggs, pickles and onion gently.
Chill at least 2 hours. Dust with paprika before serving.

title: Marry Me Chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and sear in 2 tbsp oil in an oven-safe skillet 4–5 minutes per side. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and cook the garlic, thyme and red pepper flakes 1 minute.
Stir in the broth, cream, sun-dried tomatoes and Parmesan and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken, spoon sauce over and bake 10–12 minutes until cooked through.
Top with torn basil and serve with pasta or crusty bread.

title: Cheese Dip Like Mexico Chiquito
steps: Melt the margarine in the top of a double boiler and stir in the flour to make a smooth paste.
Stir in the paprika, salt, dry mustard, chile powder, cumin and ketchup.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Add the jalapeño, jalapeño juice, grated garlic and Velveeta and stir until smooth.
Serve warm with tortilla chips.

title: Arkansas Cheese Dip
steps: Melt the butter in a small heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add the flour and stir until fully combined, about 1 minute.
Add the spices and ketchup and keep stirring for 30 seconds.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cook until slightly thickened.
Add the cheese and stir until it reaches the consistency you want. If it's too thick, add a splash of milk.

title: Pork Panang Curry
steps: Toss the pork with 1/2 tsp of the fish sauce.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the curry paste 2 minutes until fragrant, adding a splash of coconut milk if it sticks.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the torn lime leaves and palm sugar and simmer until it thickens and the oil separates.
Add the pork and simmer 3–4 minutes until just cooked. Season with the remaining fish sauce.
Serve over jasmine rice, topped with a drizzle of coconut milk, julienned lime leaves and red pepper.

title: Carolyn Garrett's Fresh Apple Cake with Caramel Frosting
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 pan.
Blend the eggs, sugar and oil. Add the dry ingredients and mix, then stir in the apples, pecans and raisins. The batter will be very thick.
Spread in the pan and bake 45–50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Frosting: boil the butter, evaporated milk and brown sugar for 3½ minutes, stirring. Add vanilla, cool, and beat until it reaches frosting consistency. Spread over the cake.

title: Brown Sugar Garlic Salmon in Foil

ingredients.name: lemon slices and parsley for garnish

title: Cathead Biscuits

ingredients.name: self-rising flour (White Lily if you can find it)

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and butter a cast iron skillet.
Whisk the flour and salt, then cut in the butter and shortening until the pieces are pea-sized.
Stir in the buttermilk with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms.
Pinch off big handfuls (cat-head size), round them gently and set them touching in the skillet.
Bake 18–22 minutes until tall and golden. Brush with melted butter.

title: Tomato Gravy
steps: Fry the bacon crisp, crumble it, and leave about 3 tbsp grease in the skillet.
Cook the onion in the grease 4 minutes, then stir in the flour for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and juice, then the milk, stirring constantly until thick, about 5 minutes.
Season with sugar, salt and pepper and stir in the bacon. Serve over hot biscuits.

title: Cheese Grits

ingredients.name: water or half water, half milk

steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil. Slowly whisk in the grits.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer 20–25 minutes (45 for stone-ground), stirring often so they don't stick.
Stir in the butter, cheese and milk until creamy. Season with pepper and cayenne.

title: Country Ham with Red-Eye Gravy
steps: Snip the fat around the edges of the ham so it doesn't curl.
Fry the ham in butter in a cast iron skillet over medium 3–4 minutes per side until browned. Move to a plate.
Pour the coffee into the hot skillet with the brown sugar and scrape up every browned bit. Boil 2 minutes.
Spoon the thin gravy over the ham, biscuits and grits.

title: Fried Apples

ingredients.name: tart apples (Granny Smith or Arkansas Black), cored and sliced

steps: Melt the butter in a cast iron skillet over medium heat.
Add the apples and cook 5 minutes, stirring.
Sprinkle with brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt, cover and cook 10 minutes until tender.
Uncover and cook until the juices are syrupy. Stir in the lemon juice.

title: Sausage Balls
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line two sheet pans with parchment.
Mix everything with your hands until evenly combined.
Roll into 1-inch balls and space them on the pans.
Bake 18–20 minutes until browned. Serve warm.

title: Sausage Hash Brown Breakfast Casserole

ingredients.name: (30 oz) frozen shredded hash browns, thawed

steps: Brown the sausage and drain. Butter a 9x13 dish.
Layer the hash browns, sausage and 1 1/2 cups cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper and pour over. Top with the remaining cheese. Refrigerate overnight if making ahead.
Bake at 350°F for 55–60 minutes until set in the center. Top with green onions and rest 10 minutes.

title: Salmon Patties

ingredients.name: (14.75 oz) pink salmon, drained, skin and big bones removed

steps: Flake the salmon, mashing the small soft bones in.
Mix in the egg, crackers, cornmeal, onion, mayo, pepper and salt.
Shape into 6 patties and chill 10 minutes.
Fry in hot oil 3–4 minutes per side until crisp. Serve with ketchup, Tartar Sauce or with grits for breakfast.

title: Fried Bologna Sandwich
steps: Cut a small slit from the edge to the center of each bologna slice so it lies flat.
Fry in a hot skillet 1–2 minutes per side until browned at the edges.
Melt the cheese on top in the last 30 seconds.
Pile on bread with mayo, mustard and onion.

title: Sweet Breakfast Rice
steps: Divide the hot rice into bowls and top each with a pat of butter.
Sprinkle with sugar and a little cinnamon.
Pour warm milk over and eat like cereal.
notes: Arkansas grows about half of America's rice, and this is how a lot of Arkansas kids grew up eating it.

title: Fried Catfish

ingredients.name: catfish fillets, cut in strips if large
lemon wedges, Tartar Sauce, hushpuppies and coleslaw

steps: Coat the catfish in the mustard and hot sauce and let it sit 15 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, seasoning, salt and pepper in a paper bag or dish.
Heat 3 inches of peanut oil to 350°F.
Shake the fish in the cornmeal mix to coat.
Fry 5–6 minutes until golden and floating. Drain on a rack and salt right away.
Serve with lemon, tartar sauce, hushpuppies and slaw.

title: Hushpuppies
steps: Whisk the dry ingredients together.
Stir in the onion, jalapeño, egg and buttermilk to make a thick batter. Rest 10 minutes.
Drop rounded tablespoons into 350°F oil (the fish oil is perfect).
Fry 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden. Drain and salt.

title: Chicken and Dumplings

ingredients.name: whole chicken (4 lb) or 3 lb bone-in thighs

steps: Simmer the chicken with the water, vegetables, salt, peppercorns and bay leaf for 1 hour.
Lift out the chicken, strain the broth and return it to the pot. Shred the meat.
Dumplings: cut the shortening into the flour, baking powder and salt, then stir in the cold broth to form a stiff dough. Roll 1/8 inch thick on a floured board and cut into 1x2-inch strips.
Bring the broth to a rolling boil and drop in the dumplings one at a time. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring gently.
Stir in the chicken, milk, butter and pepper and simmer 5 minutes until thick and creamy.

title: Southern Fried Chicken

ingredients.name: whole chicken (3 1/2 lb), cut in 8 pieces
shortening or peanut oil for frying

steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk, hot sauce and salt for 4 hours or overnight.
Mix the flour and seasonings in a paper bag.
Shake each piece in the flour, set on a rack 15 minutes, then shake again.
Heat 1 inch of shortening in a cast iron skillet to 325°F.
Fry dark meat 12–14 minutes and white meat 10–12, turning every few minutes, to 165°F (175°F for thighs).
Drain on a rack and salt lightly.

title: Smothered Pork Chops
steps: Season the chops and dredge in flour, keeping 2 tbsp of the flour.
Brown in oil 3 minutes per side and set aside.
Cook the onion in the drippings 6 minutes, sprinkle in the reserved flour and stir 1 minute.
Whisk in the broth and milk and simmer until it starts to thicken.
Return the chops, cover and simmer on low 25 minutes until tender. Serve over rice or mashed potatoes.

title: Arkansas Smoked Pulled Pork
steps: Rub the pork with mustard, coat heavily with rub and refrigerate overnight.
Smoke at 250°F over hickory, fat side up, spritzing with apple juice and vinegar every hour after the first 3 hours.
When it reaches 165°F and the bark is dark (about 6 hours), wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil.
Continue until it reaches 203°F and a probe slides in like butter, 3–4 more hours.
Rest wrapped in a cooler for at least 1 hour, then pull, discarding the bone and fat.
Serve on buns topped with slaw and sauce, the Arkansas way.

title: Delta Hot Tamales

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder or beef chuck, cut in chunks

steps: Simmer the meat in the water 2 hours until very tender. Shred it, saving the broth.
Season the meat with the filling spices and a splash of broth.
Soak the husks in hot water 30 minutes.
Beat the lard until fluffy, then add the cornmeal, baking powder, salt, chili powder and enough warm broth to make a soft dough.
Spread 2 tbsp dough on each husk, add a line of meat, roll up and fold the bottom.
Stand the tamales in a pot, add the remaining broth seasoned with more chili powder to come halfway up, cover and simmer 1 hour. Serve in their spicy juice.
notes: Delta tamales are simmered, not steamed, and are smaller and grittier than Mexican tamales — a Mississippi and Arkansas Delta tradition.

title: Sunday Pot Roast
steps: Heat the oven to 300°F. Season the roast and sear in oil in a Dutch oven 4–5 minutes per side.
Add the onion, garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes, then the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaf.
Cover and roast 2 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and carrots around the roast and cook 1 hour more until fork-tender.
Skim the juices and thicken with a cornstarch slurry for gravy if you like.

title: Pinto Beans and Ham Hocks

ingredients.name: dried pinto beans, rinsed and soaked overnight

steps: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a pot with the ham hock, onion, garlic, pepper, flakes and water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 2–2 1/2 hours until creamy, adding water as needed.
Pull the meat off the hock and return it to the pot. Season with salt.
Serve in bowls with Skillet Cornbread, chopped onion and Chow Chow.

title: Red Beans and Rice

ingredients.name: dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight

steps: Brown the sausage in a Dutch oven and set aside.
Cook the onion, pepper and celery in the drippings 8 minutes, then the garlic.
Add the beans, seasoning, bay, thyme and broth. Simmer 2 hours, stirring often.
Mash some beans against the pot to make it creamy, return the sausage and simmer 30 minutes. Season with salt.
Serve over rice with hot sauce and green onions.

title: Stuttgart Duck Gumbo

ingredients.name: wild duck breasts or 2 whole ducks, cut up
green onions, parsley and filé powder

steps: Season and brown the duck and sausage in a little oil; set aside.
Make a roux: cook the oil and flour over medium-low, stirring constantly, 30–40 minutes until the color of dark chocolate.
Stir in the onion, pepper and celery and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic.
Slowly whisk in the stock, then add the duck, sausage, seasoning, bay and thyme. Simmer 1 1/2–2 hours until the duck is tender.
Shred any whole duck off the bone, skim the fat and season. Serve over rice with green onions, parsley and a pinch of filé.
notes: Stuttgart, Arkansas is the Rice and Duck Capital of the World.

title: Bacon-Wrapped Duck Poppers
steps: Marinate the duck in Italian dressing 2–4 hours.
Fill each jalapeño half with cream cheese and lay a strip of duck on top.
Wrap tightly with bacon and secure with a toothpick.
Grill over medium indirect heat or bake at 400°F for 20–25 minutes until the bacon is crisp.

title: Venison Chili
steps: Brown the venison and pork together and drain lightly.
Add the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, then the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, beer and brown sugar and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Season and serve with cheddar, onions and cornbread.

title: Crawfish Étouffée
steps: Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 8–10 minutes to a peanut-butter-colored roux.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook 6 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste.
Slowly stir in the stock and seasoning and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the crawfish and hot sauce and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in the green onions and serve over rice.

title: Fried Frog Legs
steps: Soak the frog legs in buttermilk and hot sauce for 1 hour.
Mix the flour, cornmeal, seasoning and salt.
Dredge the legs and fry at 350°F for 5–6 minutes until golden. Serve with lemon and tartar sauce.

title: Smoked Barbecue Bologna

ingredients.name: buns, Arkansas BBQ Coleslaw and pickles

steps: Score the bologna in a 1/4-inch-deep crosshatch all over.
Coat with mustard and rub.
Smoke at 250°F for 2 1/2–3 hours until the cuts open and the outside is dark.
Glaze with sauce for the last 20 minutes. Slice thick and serve on buns with slaw.

title: Fried Chicken Livers
steps: Soak the livers in buttermilk for 1 hour. Prick each one with a fork to keep them from popping.
Dredge in seasoned flour.
Fry at 350°F (use a splatter screen) for 3–4 minutes until crisp and just cooked through. Serve with hot sauce or white gravy.

title: Chicken Fried Steak
steps: Season the steaks. Mix the flour with garlic powder and paprika. Whisk the eggs and buttermilk.
Dredge in flour, dip in the egg wash, then press firmly into the flour again.
Fry in 1/2 inch of 350°F oil 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
Pour off all but 1/3 cup oil, make the white gravy in the pan, and smother.

title: Fried Okra
steps: Soak the okra in buttermilk 10 minutes.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and toss in the cornmeal, flour and seasonings.
Fry in batches in 350°F oil 3–4 minutes until golden. Drain and salt while hot.

title: Purple Hull Peas

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen purple hull peas (shelled)
bacon or a smoked ham hock

steps: Cook the bacon in a pot until it renders, then add the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the peas, water, pepper and sugar. Simmer partly covered 45 minutes until tender.
Season with salt. Serve with cornbread, sliced tomatoes and chopped onion.
notes: Emerson, Arkansas holds the Purple Hull Pea Festival every June.

title: Black-Eyed Peas

ingredients.name: smoked ham hock or 1/2 lb diced ham

steps: Put everything except the salt in a pot and bring to a boil.
Simmer 1–1 1/2 hours until creamy and tender, adding water as needed.
Pull the meat from the hock, return it, and season with salt. Serve with cornbread and Pepper Sauce.

title: Turnip Greens

ingredients.name: turnip greens (with roots if you have them), washed well
smoked ham hock or 6 slice bacon

steps: Simmer the ham hock in the water 30 minutes to make a pot likker.
Strip the greens from the thick stems, tear them up and add with the sugar, salt and pepper flakes.
Simmer 45 minutes, adding the turnip roots for the last 20 minutes.
Serve with Pepper Sauce and cornbread for dunking in the likker.

title: Fried Cabbage
steps: Fry the bacon until crisp in a large skillet; keep the grease.
Cook the onion 5 minutes, then add the cabbage, salt, pepper, flakes and sugar.
Cook 12–15 minutes, stirring, until tender with browned edges. Stir in the vinegar and bacon.

title: Skillet Fried Corn
steps: Cut the kernels off the cob, then scrape the cobs with the back of the knife to get the milk.
Melt the butter in a cast iron skillet over medium heat and add the corn.
Cook 10 minutes, stirring, then sprinkle in the flour and add the milk, sugar, salt and pepper.
Simmer 5 minutes until creamy.

title: Stewed Okra and Tomatoes
steps: Cook the bacon, crumble it, and keep the grease.
Cook the onion in the grease 4 minutes, then add the okra for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, corn, salt, pepper and sugar and simmer 15 minutes. Top with the bacon. Serve over rice.

title: Arkansas BBQ Coleslaw
steps: Whisk the mayo, vinegar, sugar, mustard, celery seed, salt and pepper.
Toss with the slaw and chill 1 hour. Pile it on pulled pork sandwiches.

title: Hot Water Cornbread
steps: Mix the cornmeal, salt, sugar and butter.
Pour in the boiling water and stir to a thick, moldable dough. Rest 5 minutes.
With wet hands, shape into small flat patties.
Fry in 1/2 inch of hot oil 3 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Serve with greens and beans.

title: Dirty Rice
steps: Brown the meat and livers in a large skillet.
Add the onion, pepper and celery for 6 minutes, then the garlic and seasoning.
Stir in the rice to coat, add the broth, cover and simmer 18 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff, and fold in the green onions.

title: Tomato Pie
steps: Salt the tomato slices and drain on paper towels 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Layer the tomatoes, basil and green onions in the crust.
Mix the cheeses, mayo and pepper and spread over the top to the edges.
Bake 30–35 minutes until golden. Rest 20 minutes before slicing.

title: Bradley County Pink Tomato Sandwich

ingredients.name: large ripe Bradley County pink tomato

steps: Slice the tomato thick.
Spread mayo edge to edge on all four slices.
Layer the tomato, salt and pepper it generously, and close. Eat over the sink.
notes: Warren, Arkansas holds the Bradley County Pink Tomato Festival each June.

title: Pimento Cheese
steps: Mix everything until well combined but still chunky.
Chill 1 hour. Serve on crackers, celery, white bread or burgers.

title: Pickled Okra
steps: Pack the okra upright in 4 clean pint jars with a garlic clove, pepper and 1/2 tsp dill seed each.
Boil the vinegar, water and salt and pour over to within 1/2 inch of the top.
Seal and process in a boiling water bath 10 minutes, or refrigerate and eat within a month. Wait 2 weeks before opening.

title: Chow Chow
steps: Toss the vegetables with salt and let them sit overnight in the fridge. Rinse and drain well.
Boil the vinegar, sugar and spices, add the vegetables and simmer 10 minutes.
Pack into clean jars and refrigerate (or process 10 minutes to store). Spoon over beans and greens.

title: Pepper Sauce

ingredients.name: small hot peppers (tabasco, serrano or bird peppers)

steps: Pack the peppers into a clean bottle or jar, poking each with a toothpick.
Heat the vinegar and salt until steaming and pour over the peppers.
Cap and let it sit 2 weeks. Shake over greens and peas, and top up with vinegar as you use it.

title: Arkansas Barbecue Sauce
steps: Whisk everything in a saucepan and simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring.
Cool and refrigerate up to a month.

title: Fig Preserves
steps: Combine everything in a heavy pot and let it sit 1 hour until juicy.
Simmer, stirring often, 60–75 minutes until thick and jammy.
Ladle into clean jars and refrigerate, or process 10 minutes. Spread on hot biscuits.

title: Sweet Tea
steps: Bring 4 cups water to a boil, remove from heat and add the tea bags and baking soda. Steep 15 minutes.
Remove the bags without squeezing and stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Pour into a pitcher with 4 cups cold water and chill. Serve over lots of ice with lemon.

title: Arkansas Fried Pies
steps: Simmer the fruit in the water 30–40 minutes until soft and thick. Mash, stir in the sugar, cinnamon and butter, and cool.
Cut the shortening into the flour and salt and stir in the milk to form a dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll thin and cut 6-inch circles. Spoon 2 tbsp filling on each, fold over and crimp with a fork.
Fry in 350°F oil 2 minutes per side until golden. Drain and dust with powdered sugar.
notes: Fried pie stands dot Arkansas highways, especially around Mount Nebo and the Ozarks.

title: Possum Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the flour, butter and pecans, press into a 9x13 pan and bake 20 minutes. Cool.
Beat the cream cheese and powdered sugar, fold in 1 cup whipped topping and spread over the crust.
Whisk both puddings with the milk 2 minutes until thick and spread over the cream cheese layer.
Top with the remaining whipped topping, toasted pecans and chocolate shavings. Chill 4 hours.
notes: Called possum pie because it "plays possum" — the chocolate hides under the whipped topping.

title: Blackberry Cobbler
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Toss the berries with 1 cup sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice.
Melt the butter in a 9x13 dish in the oven.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and milk and pour over the melted butter without stirring.
Spoon the berries over the batter.
Bake 45–50 minutes until the crust rises up golden around the fruit. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

title: Peach Cobbler

ingredients.name: sliced fresh peaches (Johnson County if you can)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Simmer the peaches with 1 cup sugar and cinnamon 5 minutes; stir in the vanilla.
Melt the butter in a 9x13 dish in the oven.
Whisk the self-rising flour, sugar and milk and pour over the butter without stirring.
Spoon the peaches and juice over the batter.
Bake 45 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: Clarksville holds the Johnson County Peach Festival, Arkansas's oldest festival.

title: Banana Pudding
steps: Whisk the sugar, flour and salt in a saucepan, then whisk in the milk and yolks.
Cook over medium, whisking constantly, until thick like pudding, 8–10 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the butter and vanilla.
Layer wafers, bananas and warm custard in a 2-quart dish, ending with custard.
Beat the whites to soft peaks, add the sugar gradually and beat to stiff peaks. Spread over to the edges.
Bake at 375°F for 10 minutes until golden. Serve warm or chilled.

title: Buttermilk Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Whisk the butter, sugar and flour, then the eggs one at a time.
Whisk in the buttermilk, vanilla, lemon juice and nutmeg.
Pour into the crust and bake 50–55 minutes until set with a slight jiggle. Cool completely.

title: Coconut Cream Pie

ingredients.name: sweetened flaked coconut, plus 1/4 cup toasted

steps: Whisk the sugar, cornstarch, salt, milk and yolks in a saucepan and cook over medium, stirring, until thick and bubbling. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the butter, vanilla and 1 cup coconut and pour into the crust.
Beat the whites to stiff peaks with the sugar and spread over the hot filling, sealing the edges.
Sprinkle with toasted coconut and bake at 350°F for 12–15 minutes. Cool, then chill 4 hours.

title: Strawberry Shortcake

ingredients.name: heavy cream, whipped with 2 tbsp sugar

steps: Toss the berries with sugar and let them sit 30 minutes to get juicy.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the butter into the flour and sugar, stir in the cream, pat 3/4 inch thick and cut 8 biscuits.
Bake 12–15 minutes until golden.
Split the warm biscuits and fill with berries, juice and whipped cream.
notes: Bald Knob, Arkansas has held a Strawberry Festival since the 1930s.

title: Old-Fashioned Chocolate Fudge
steps: Butter a 9x9 pan.
Bring the sugar, butter and evaporated milk to a full rolling boil, stirring constantly, and boil 4 minutes (to 234°F).
Off the heat, stir in the chocolate until melted, then the marshmallow creme, vanilla and pecans.
Spread in the pan and cool completely before cutting into squares.

title: Southern Rice Pudding
steps: Simmer the rice in the water 15 minutes until absorbed.
Add the milk, sugar and salt and simmer gently 20 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Temper the beaten eggs with a ladle of hot rice, stir back in and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir in the vanilla and raisins. Dust with cinnamon and nutmeg. Serve warm or cold.

title: Classic Roast Turkey

ingredients.name: whole turkey (12–14 lb), thawed, giblets removed and saved

steps: Two or three days ahead: pat the turkey dry, rub the dry brine all over and under the breast skin, and refrigerate uncovered on a rack.
Take it out 1 hour before roasting. Heat the oven to 425°F.
Rub the butter under and over the skin. Stuff the cavity with onion, lemon, garlic and herbs. Tuck the wings and tie the legs.
Roast on a rack over the stock for 30 minutes, then lower to 325°F.
Roast about 13 minutes per pound total, basting every 45 minutes and tenting the breast with foil once golden, until the thigh reads 170°F and the breast 160°F.
Rest at least 30 minutes before carving. Save the drippings for Giblet Gravy.

title: Cajun Fried Turkey

ingredients.name: whole turkey (12–14 lb), thawed and very dry, giblets removed

steps: Measure the oil first: put the turkey in the empty pot, cover with water by 1 inch, remove the turkey and mark the water line. Dry the pot and turkey completely.
Strain the injection (butter, broth, hot sauce, Worcestershire, 1 tbsp seasoning) and inject all over the breast, thighs and legs. Rub the rest of the seasoning on the skin. Refrigerate overnight.
Outdoors, away from the house, on level ground: heat the oil to 350°F.
Turn the burner off, lower the turkey in very slowly on the hook, then relight and keep the oil at 325–350°F.
Fry 3 1/2 minutes per pound until the breast reads 160°F and thigh 175°F.
Lift out slowly, drain and rest 20 minutes before carving.
notes: Never fry a frozen or wet turkey, never fry indoors or on a deck, and keep a fire extinguisher close.

title: Turkey Stock

ingredients.name: turkey neck, back and giblets (not the liver)

steps: Brown the neck and giblets in oil in a stockpot.
Add the vegetables, bay, peppercorns, parsley and water.
Simmer gently 2–3 hours, skimming. Strain and save the giblets for gravy. Keeps 4 days or freeze.

title: Giblet Gravy

ingredients.name: cooked giblets and neck meat, finely chopped

steps: Pour the drippings into a cup and spoon off the fat; use it in place of some of the butter.
Melt the butter and fat in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook 3–4 minutes until golden.
Slowly whisk in the stock and the defatted drippings and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Stir in the giblets, eggs, salt, pepper and poultry seasoning. Thin with stock as needed.

title: Cornbread Dressing

ingredients.name: recipe Skillet Cornbread, baked a day ahead and crumbled

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13 dish.
Melt the butter and cook the onion and celery 8–10 minutes until soft.
In a big bowl, combine the cornbread, bread, vegetables and seasonings.
Stir in the stock and soup until very moist — it should look like thick oatmeal. Taste for seasoning, then stir in the eggs.
Spread in the dish and bake 45–55 minutes until set and golden on top.

title: Oyster Dressing
steps: Make the Cornbread Dressing mixture, using the oyster liquor for part of the stock.
Fold in the oysters, parsley and green onions.
Bake at 350°F for 50–60 minutes until set.

title: Cranberry Sauce
steps: Simmer everything 10–12 minutes until most of the berries pop.
Cool — it thickens as it sets. Make up to 5 days ahead.

title: Sweet Potato Casserole
steps: Bake the sweet potatoes at 400°F for 1 hour until soft. Cool, peel and mash.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Beat in the sugar, butter, eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt and spread in a 9x13 dish.
Mix the brown sugar, flour, butter and pecans and crumble over the top.
Bake 30 minutes. For marshmallows, scatter them on for the last 10 minutes.

title: Candied Yams

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/2 inch thick

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and arrange the slices in a 9x13 dish.
Melt the butter with the sugars and spices until bubbling, then stir in the vanilla.
Pour over the potatoes, cover with foil and bake 40 minutes.
Uncover, baste with the syrup and bake 20–25 minutes more until tender and glazed.

title: Green Bean Casserole

ingredients.name: fresh green beans, trimmed and blanched (or 4 cans, drained)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Cook the mushrooms in butter 6 minutes, add the garlic, then the flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in the broth and half-and-half and simmer until thick. Season with soy, pepper and salt.
Fold in the beans and half the onions and pour into a dish.
Bake 20 minutes, top with the remaining onions and bake 5 more.

title: Collard Greens

ingredients.name: smoked turkey wings or 1 ham hock
collard greens, stemmed, washed and sliced

steps: Simmer the smoked meat with the water, onion and garlic for 45 minutes.
Add the greens a few handfuls at a time, with the sugar and pepper flakes.
Simmer 1–1 1/2 hours until silky. Pull the meat off the bone and return it.
Stir in the vinegar and salt. Serve with Pepper Sauce.

title: Yeast Dinner Rolls

ingredients.name: butter, melted, plus more for brushing

steps: Stir the milk, water, yeast and sugar and let it foam 5 minutes.
Mix in the butter, eggs and salt, then the flour a cup at a time to a soft dough. Knead 6–8 minutes.
Cover and let rise 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Shape into 24 balls and set in two buttered 9x13 pans. Rise 45 minutes.
Bake at 375°F for 15–18 minutes until golden. Brush with butter.

title: Broccoli Rice Casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13 dish.
Cook the onion in butter 5 minutes, then stir in the soups, Velveeta and milk until melted.
Fold in the rice and broccoli and spread in the dish. Top with cheddar and crackers tossed in butter.
Bake 30–35 minutes until bubbling.

title: Squash Casserole
steps: Simmer the squash and onion in the water 10 minutes until tender. Drain very well and mash lightly.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Stir in half the butter, the eggs, mayo, cheese, salt and pepper.
Spread in a 2-quart dish, top with crackers tossed in the remaining butter.
Bake 30–35 minutes until golden.

title: Corn Pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x9 dish.
Stir everything together and pour into the dish.
Bake 45–50 minutes until golden and just set in the middle.

title: Brown Sugar Glazed Ham
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Put the ham cut side down in a roasting pan with 1/2 cup water, cover tightly with foil.
Bake about 12 minutes per pound until 120°F inside.
Simmer the brown sugar, honey, mustard, juice and spices 3 minutes for the glaze.
Raise the oven to 400°F, brush the ham with glaze and bake uncovered 15–20 minutes, glazing twice more, until caramelized.

title: Pecan Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Whisk the corn syrup, brown sugar, eggs, butter, vanilla and salt.
Spread the pecans in the crust and pour the filling over.
Bake 55–65 minutes until set with a slight jiggle, covering the crust edge with foil if it browns fast. Cool 3 hours.

title: Pumpkin Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Whisk everything until smooth and pour into the crust.
Bake 15 minutes, lower to 350°F and bake 40–45 minutes until the center is just set.
Cool completely and serve with whipped cream.

title: Sweet Potato Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Beat the sweet potatoes and butter until smooth, then beat in everything else.
Pour into the crust and bake 55–60 minutes until a knife comes out clean. Cool.

title: Chess Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Whisk the sugar, cornmeal, flour and salt, then the butter, milk, vinegar and vanilla.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time and pour into the crust.
Bake 45–50 minutes until golden and set. Cool completely.

title: Strawberry Pretzel Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the pretzels, butter and sugar, press into a 9x13 dish and bake 10 minutes. Cool.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar, fold in the whipped topping and spread over the crust, sealing the edges.
Dissolve the gelatin in boiling water, stir in the strawberries and chill until slightly thick, about 30 minutes.
Pour over the cream layer and chill 4 hours until set.

title: Ambrosia

ingredients.name: (10 oz) maraschino cherries, drained and halved

steps: Fold the sour cream and whipped topping together.
Fold in the fruit, marshmallows, coconut and pecans.
Chill at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Pecan Pralines
steps: Line a sheet pan with parchment.
Bring the sugars, milk and butter to a boil, stirring, and cook to 238°F (soft ball).
Off the heat, stir in the pecans and vanilla and beat 2–3 minutes until it thickens and turns cloudy.
Drop by spoonfuls onto the parchment quickly and let set 30 minutes.

title: Divinity
steps: Make this on a dry, low-humidity day. Line pans with wax paper.
Cook the sugar, corn syrup and water to 260°F without stirring.
Meanwhile beat the egg whites to stiff peaks. With the mixer running, pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream.
Beat 5–6 minutes until it holds its shape and loses its gloss. Fold in the vanilla and pecans.
Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper and let set.

title: Peanut Brittle
steps: Butter a sheet pan.
Cook the sugar, corn syrup and water to 240°F, add the peanuts and cook, stirring, to 300°F.
Off the heat, quickly stir in the butter and vanilla, then the baking soda — it will foam.
Pour onto the pan and spread thin. Cool and break into pieces.

title: Turkey Tetrazzini
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Cook the spaghetti 2 minutes short of done.
Cook the mushrooms and onion in butter 8 minutes, stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock and milk and simmer until thick.
Stir in the Parmesan, turkey, peas, salt and pepper, then the pasta.
Spread in a 9x13 dish, top with mozzarella and bake 25 minutes until bubbly.

title: Southern Macaroni Salad
steps: Cook the macaroni in well-salted water until just tender. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, relish, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Fold in the macaroni, eggs, celery, bell pepper and onion.
Chill at least 2 hours. Stir, loosen with a spoonful of mayo if needed, and dust with paprika.

title: Seven-Layer Salad
steps: Layer the lettuce, celery, onion, bell pepper and peas in a clear trifle bowl or 9x13 dish.
Stir the mayonnaise and sugar together and spread it over the peas, sealing to the edges.
Top with the cheddar, bacon and eggs. Cover and chill overnight. Toss at the table or serve in layers.

title: Broccoli Salad with Bacon
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, sugar, vinegar and salt.
Toss with the broccoli, onion, raisins and seeds or pecans.
Chill 1 hour, then fold in the bacon just before serving.

title: Cucumber, Tomato and Onion Salad
steps: Stir the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the cucumbers, tomatoes and onion. Chill at least 30 minutes, tossing once.

title: Classic Wedge Salad
steps: Set a cold wedge on each plate.
Spoon the dressing over, then top with blue cheese, bacon, tomatoes, chives and cracked pepper.

title: Cornbread Salad

ingredients.name: recipe skillet cornbread, baked a day ahead and crumbled
(15 oz) pinto beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream and ranch seasoning.
In a trifle bowl, layer half the cornbread, beans, corn, tomatoes, bell pepper, green onions, cheese, bacon and dressing. Repeat.
Cover and chill at least 3 hours so the cornbread soaks up the dressing.

title: English Pea Salad
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, sour cream, sugar, salt and pepper.
Fold in the peas, cheese, onion and eggs. Chill 1 hour and top with bacon.

title: Southern Garden Salad with Buttermilk Ranch

ingredients.name: iceberg or green leaf lettuce, chopped

steps: Whisk the buttermilk, mayonnaise, sour cream, herbs and seasonings. Chill 30 minutes to thicken.
Toss the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, carrots and onion. Top with croutons and serve the ranch on the side.

title: Pickled Beet and Onion Salad

ingredients.name: (15 oz) sliced beets, drained (save 1/2 cup juice)

steps: Bring the beet juice, vinegar, sugar, cloves and salt to a simmer, stirring to dissolve.
Pour over the beets and onion in a jar. Chill overnight.

title: Black-Eyed Pea Salad

ingredients.name: (15 oz) black-eyed peas, drained and rinsed

steps: Toss everything together.
Chill at least 2 hours. Serve with tortilla chips or as a side.

title: Angel Biscuits
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Cut in the shortening until crumbly.
Stir in the buttermilk and yeast just until a dough forms. (Cover and chill up to 5 days if you like.)
Roll 1/2 inch thick on a floured board, cut with a biscuit cutter and set on a buttered sheet. Let rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 425°F for 10–12 minutes. Brush with melted butter.

title: Buttermilk Corn Muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and grease a muffin tin.
Whisk the dry ingredients. Whisk the eggs, buttermilk and butter, then stir into the dry just until combined.
Fill the cups 2/3 full and bake 14–16 minutes, until golden.

title: Garlic Texas Toast
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Mash the butter, garlic, parsley and parmesan. Spread on both sides of the bread.
Bake on a sheet pan 5 minutes, flip, and bake 3–5 minutes more until golden.

title: Sweet Potato Biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Whisk the sweet potato and buttermilk. Mix the flour, brown sugar and cinnamon, then cut in the butter.
Stir in the sweet potato mixture until just combined. Pat 3/4 inch thick and cut into rounds.
Bake 12–14 minutes until the bottoms are golden.

title: Southern Spoon Bread
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a 2-quart dish.
Scald the milk, whisk in the cornmeal and salt, and cook, stirring, until thick like grits. Stir in the butter and cool 10 minutes.
Stir in the yolks and baking powder. Beat the whites to soft peaks and fold in.
Bake 35–40 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve with a spoon, right away.

title: Southern Green Beans

ingredients.name: fresh green beans, trimmed and snapped

steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot until crisp. Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic for a minute.
Add the beans, broth, sugar, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer low 1 hour, until very tender.

title: Southern Creamed Corn

ingredients.name: ears fresh sweet corn, kernels cut and cobs scraped (or 5 cups frozen)

steps: Melt the butter in a skillet, add the corn and its milky scrapings, and cook 5 minutes.
Whisk the cream, milk, sugar and flour; stir into the corn with the salt and pepper.
Simmer, stirring, 10–15 minutes until thick and creamy.

title: Southern Butter Beans

ingredients.name: smoked ham hock or 4 slice bacon

steps: Simmer the ham hock and onion in the broth for 20 minutes.
Add the butter beans and simmer 30–40 minutes until creamy and tender. Stir in the butter, salt and pepper.

title: Honey Glazed Carrots
steps: Boil the carrots in salted water 6–8 minutes until just tender. Drain.
Melt the butter, honey and brown sugar in the pot, return the carrots and toss over medium heat until glazed. Season and top with parsley.

title: Southern Pinto Beans

ingredients.name: dried pinto beans, rinsed and soaked overnight

steps: Drain the beans and add to a pot with the ham hock, onion, garlic and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 2 1/2–3 hours until creamy, adding water as needed.
Pull the meat from the hock, return it to the pot and season. Serve with cornbread and chopped onion.

title: Southern Baked Beans
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Cook the bacon until half done, then the onion and pepper until soft.
Stir everything together in a 9x13 dish.
Bake uncovered 1 hour, until thick and bubbling.

title: Sautéed Squash and Onions
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet and cook the onion 5 minutes.
Add the squash, salt and pepper and cook, stirring now and then, 10–12 minutes until tender and lightly browned.

title: Fried Cornbread (Hoecakes)
steps: Whisk everything except the oil into a pourable batter.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a cast iron skillet. Fry 1/4-cup cakes about 2 minutes a side until crisp and golden.
